t.1.3.1: But the righteous-souled one, having heard that entire account of yours, which was in harmony with dharma, sought once more to learn clearly all that had befallen that wise one.
t.1.3.2: Having sipped water, the sage, collecting himself, took his place with joined palms on darbha grass whose tips pointed east, and through the power of dharma sought out the course of the story.
t.1.3.3: The birth of Rāma, his exceedingly great valor, his kindness toward all, his being beloved of the world, his forbearance, his gentleness, and his truthful character.
t.1.3.4: And other varied and wondrous tales from the time of journeying with Viśvāmitra, and the marriage of Jānakī, and the breaking of the bow.
t.1.3.6: And the obstruction of the consecration, and the banishment of Rāma, the grief and lamentation of the king, and his resort to the other world.
t.1.3.5: He beheld the dispute between Rāma and Rāma, and likewise the virtues of Dāśarathi; likewise too the consecration of Rāma and the wicked disposition of Kaikeyī.
t.1.3.7: The grief of the subjects and the sending away of the subjects, the conversation with the lord of the Niṣādas, and likewise the return of the charioteer.
t.1.3.8: The crossing over from the Gaṅgā, the meeting with Bharadvāja, and, by Bharadvāja's leave, the sight of Citrakūṭa.
t.1.3.10: And the consecration of the excellent sandals, the dwelling at Nandigrāma, the journey into the Daṇḍaka forest, and the meeting with Sutīkṣṇa.
t.1.3.9: The construction of the dwelling and the settling in it, likewise the arrival of Bharata, the entreaty to win Rāma's favour, and the water-offering rite for his father.
t.1.3.12: The slaying of Khara and Triśiras, and the rising up of Rāvaṇa, and likewise the slaying of Mārīca, and also the abduction of Vaidehī.
t.1.3.11: The meeting with Anasūyā and the offering of the fragrant body-unguent, the conversation of Śūrpaṇakhā, and likewise her disfigurement.
t.1.3.13: And the lament of Rāghava, the slaying of the king of vultures, the sighting of Kabandha, and also the sight of Pampā.
t.1.3.14: He depicted the meeting with Śabarī, and likewise the meeting with Hanumān, and the lament of the great-souled Rāghava at Pampā.
t.1.3.15: He described the going to Ṛṣyamūka, the meeting with Sugrīva, the producing of trust, the friendship, and the conflict between Vālin and Sugrīva.
t.1.3.16: The crushing of Vālin and the installing of Sugrīva, the time of Tārā's lamentation, and the dwelling through the nights of the rainy season.
t.1.3.17: The wrath of Rāghava, lion among men, the gathering of the forces, the dispatching of the monkeys to the quarters, and the description of the earth.
t.1.3.18: He told of the giving of the signet ring, the discovery of the bear's cave, the vow of fasting unto death, and also the meeting with Sampāti.
t.1.3.20: His going to the drinking hall, his seeing of the women's quarters, his going to the aśoka grove, and also his seeing of Sītā.
t.1.3.19: The climbing of the mountain and the leaping across the ocean, the entry into Laṅkā by night, and the anxious reflection of the one who was all alone.
t.1.3.21: He also composed the giving of the token of recognition, Sītā's speech, the threatening by the rākṣasīs, and Trijaṭā's seeing of a dream.
t.1.3.22: Sītā's giving of the jewel, and likewise the breaking of the trees, the flight of the rākṣasīs, and the slaying of the Kiṃkaras.
t.1.3.23: The seizing of the son of Vāyu, and his roaring at the burning of Laṅkā, then the leaping back across the sea, and likewise the carrying off of the honey.
t.1.3.24: The consoling of Rāghava, likewise the handing over of the jewel, the meeting with the ocean, and the building of Nala's bridge.
t.1.3.26: The death of Kumbhakarṇa, the slaying of Meghanāda, the destruction of Rāvaṇa, and the recovery of Sītā in the city of the enemy.
t.1.3.25: The crossing of the ocean, the siege of Laṅkā by night, the alliance with Vibhīṣaṇa, and the disclosure of the means of slaying the foe.
t.1.3.27: And the consecration of Vibhīṣaṇa, and the sight of the Puṣpaka, and the going to Ayodhyā, and the reunion with Bharata.
t.1.3.28: The festive celebration of Rāma's consecration, the dismissal of all the armies, the gladdening of his own kingdom, and the sending away of Vaidehī.
t.1.3.29: And whatever of Rāma's deeds on the face of the earth had not yet come to pass, that too the blessed sage Vālmīki set down in the latter part of his poem.
